author: jasonruonanwang
body:
Fixes #3151

It seems that GCC 10 handles template instantiation differently from previous GCC versions, and as a result, some template instantiation in DataMan serializer failed to pick up the correct template instantiation. This PR changed the affected template instantiation to simple function overloading.

author: arcum42
body:
### Description of Changes
The help menu was reformatted, and now shows flags that were there, but not shown.

The switch_wxconfig function has been removed.

### Rationale behind Changes
The command used in switch_wxconfig was debian/ubuntu specific, and was specifying to switch to the *gtk 2* version of wx, which we don't want. With 32 bits removed, we don't really have to worry as much about having both a 32 and 64 bit version of wx on the system.

### Suggested Testing Steps
Compile with build.sh and make sure it works, especially on a debian/ubuntu based distribution.

body:
## Done

- Increased space for tag names in machine tag form
- Moved Automatic tags help text underneath the table, otherwise it gets super squished. @huwshimi the Zeplin wireframe shows this version as well as the version where it's in the table cell - not sure which one has the right text?

## QA

### MAAS deployment

To run this branch you will need access to one of the following MAAS deployments:

- [Karura](/HACKING.md#karura)
- [Bolla](/HACKING.md#bolla)
- [A development MAAS](/HACKING.md#development-deployment)
- [A local snap MAAS](/HACKING.md#snap-deployment) (this will not usually have machines)

### Running the branch

You can run this branch by:

- Serving with [dotrun](/HACKING.md#maas-ui-development-setup)
- [Building in a development MAAS](/HACKING.md#running-maas-ui-from-a-development-maas)

### QA steps

- Go to the machine list, select some machines and select "Tag" from the action menu
- Check that the tag name has more space than before at all screen sizes

## Fixes

Fixes canonical-web-and-design/app-tribe#792

author: oriolabril
body:
You can check the preview in the checks section below. I think this will make the blog "publishable". The changes are:
* I have added an intro about the PyMC project and its activities beyond developing the PyMC library
* I have updated the announcements
* I have moved some of the content from the About section of the docs (if we have it here we can remove it from the versioned docs and convert in to an external link pointing to this website)
* I have copied the notebook from https://github.com/pymc-devs/pymc-examples/pull/303 here. I have only added a post directive to it, everything else, text, code and outputs is untouched.
* I extended the external links section
* (infrastructure only) I have removed the github pages workflow as it was not needed, readthedocs already builds both main website and PR previews and is easier to maintain

There is no need to keep all the changes, we can go back to a blog scope only for example. cc @twiecki @mjhajharia @reshamas

Things that need to be decided:
* Scope of the website: blog only or project info + blog?
* ~url of the website. The idea is to [host this at `pymc.io`](https://discourse.pymc.io/t/proposal-create-a-page-pymc-io-which-acts-as-a-news-feed-for-pymc/8661) and this hasn't changed, but readthedocs by default adds the `/en/latest/` suffix to the url.~ 
  
  ~This can be configured and removed to host a versionless page, but it's either both present or none present. versions make no sense here, so the `latest` is useless, but if we choose the versionless mode, the `en` will also go and we won't be able to translate the website~
  - Note: translating sphinx generated websites is not complicated, I tried it out at https://sphinx-primer.readthedocs.io/ca/latest/ (you can see it now has a catalan version) using [transifex](https://www.transifex.com/arviz/sphinx-primer-website/dashboard/).

Things that need to be done:
* @twiecki has to make the url decision above a reality once we choose something (I already made you a maintainer of https://readthedocs.org/projects/pymcio/)

author: berniewhite
body:
## PR Summary

What's changed since v1.13.4:

- New features:
  - Added support for referencing resources in template. #1315
    - The `reference()` function can be used to reference resources in template.
    - A placeholder value is still used for resources outside of the template.
  - Added March 2022 baselines `Azure.GA_2022_03` and `Azure.Preview_2022_03`. #1334
    - Includes rules released before or during March 2022.
    - Marked `Azure.GA_2021_12` and `Azure.Preview_2021_12` baselines as obsolete.
  - **Experimental**: Cmdlets to validate objects with Azure policy conditions:
    - `Export-AzPolicyAssignmentData` - Exports policy assignment data. #1266
    - `Export-AzPolicyAssignmentRuleData` - Exports JSON rules from policy assignment data. #1278
    - `Get-AzPolicyAssignmentDataSource` - Discovers policy assignment data. #1340
    - See cmdlet help for limitations and usage.
- New rules:
  - SignalR Service:
    - Check services use Managed Identities. #1306
    - Check services use a SKU with an SLA. #1307
  - Web PubSub Service:
    - Check services use Managed Identities. #1308
    - Check services use a SKU with an SLA. #1309
- Updated rules:
  - Azure Kubernetes Service:
    - Updated `Azure.AKS.Version` to use latest stable version `1.21.9`. #1318
      - Use `AZURE_AKS_CLUSTER_MINIMUM_VERSION` to configure the minimum version of the cluster.
- Engineering:
  - Cache Azure Policy Aliases. #1277
  - Cleanup of additional alias metadata. #1351
- Bug fixes:
  - Fixed index was out of range with split on mock properties. #1327
  - Fixed mock objects with no properties. #1347
  - Fixed sub-resources nesting by scope regression. #1348
  - Fixed expand of runtime properties on reference objects. #1324
  - Fixed processing of deployment outputs. #1316

What's changed since pre-release v1.14.0-B2204013:

- No additional changes.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR has a meaningful title
- [x] Summarized changes
- [x] Change is not breaking
- [x] This PR is ready to merge and is not **Work in Progress**

author: postmodern
body:
1. Added a `.gemspec` file based on the gem metadata of [evil-win-3.3](https://rubygems.org/gems/evil-winrm/versions/3.3). Also added additional project metadata (`changelog_uri` and `source_code_uri`).
2. Restrict dependency versions to `~> X.Y, >= X.Y.Z`. This silences warnings from `gem build evil-winrm.gemspec`.
3. Added the [readline](https://rubygems.org/gems/readline) gem as a dependency. If Ruby is not built with `libreadline` support, the `Readline` module will actually point to the `Reline` module provided by the new [reline](https://rubygems.org/gems/reline) gem. `reline` is a pure-Ruby alternative to GNU readline, but does not support all of `Readline`'s methods (ex: `quoting_detection_proc`). This ensures that `Readline` always points to the actual `Readline`; although you should consider switching to `reline` to avoid any `readline` compilation issues.
4. Added bundler as development dependency.
5. Changed the `Gemfile` to pull dependencies in from the `evil-winrm.gemspec` file.
6. Removed the `Gemfile.lock` file, as it's typically only committed to Git for web applications, not for CLI utils.

author: gsoltis
body:
This PR is a proposal for how we can start to get a handle on the various kinds of paths that `turbo` uses.

My goal is the following:
 * Eventually ensure that an absolute, platform-dependent path is used any time we interact with the filesystem
   * This will allow us to guarantee that we don't break `--cwd`, which is likely currently broken
 * Eventually ensure that we can easily identify relative paths, both with respect to the monorepo root and to a particular package root
 * Be incrementally adoptable. There is a huge amount of surface area to this change, so it's important to be able to tackle it a piece at a time
 * Be auditable. The goal would be to eventually ban usage of `path/filepath` and a subset of `os.*` functions anywhere in the codebase outside `path.go`. It may even be possible to automate this in CI. Furthermore, entry points and exit points from our custom types (currently just `AbsolutePath`) are clearly marked, along with the intention of eventually migrating them, if appropriate (e.g. `ToStringDuringMigration`, `UnsafeToAbsolutePath`).
 * New PRs that interact with the filesystem should use `fs.AbsolutePath`, even if they need to use one of the migration functions to facilitate that. Hopefully this will force both the submitter and reviewer to focus on ensuring that the new code will work properly with `--cwd`.

I've done a few pieces of the migration to show what it would look like in the code base in a partially migrated state. `path.go` contains the `AbsolutePath` type, which ideally would be the sole way to interact with the filesystem. Please let me know what you think about the api and the migration overall.

This diff expands on https://github.com/oxidecomputer/cobble-build/pull/3, allowing arguments to be passed when running the outputs. Examples:
```
./cobble run -v cobalt//hdl:InitialResetTest#script --help
./cobble run -v cobalt//hdl:InitialResetTest#script -V initial_reset.vcd
```

This can also be reversed, interpreting the remainder of the arguments after the query as command (and arguments) to be invoked and passing the outputs as arguments instead. This makes it easier to incorporate Cobble with additional tools to process generated outputs. Example:

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR introduces two new kinds of histograms, weighted histograms and timing histograms.  A timing histogram has the interface of a gauge, but keeps track of the time that the variable spent in each of the ranges defined by the bucket boundaries.  A timing histogram is built on a weighted histogram, which is like a regular histogram but its Observe method takes a weight as well as a value.  Due to the limitations of the current model (in OpenMetrics) for histograms, the weight has to be an unsigned integer.  The timing histograms are intended to replace the existing sample-and-watermark histograms in k/apiserver/pkg/util/flowcontrol with something less complex to consume and less costly at runtime to update.

These new histograms are hoped to eventually migrate into prometheus. Until then, they resides in k/component-base/metrics/prometheusextension .

author: laurilano
body:
For a string ID, for example "Muller2019", passed to DataServer without an internet connection, DataServer will now attempt to find a version of the Müller et al. 2019 plate model files on the GPlately cache and return it to the user. If it has not been cached before, a ConnectionError will be raised.

If changes have been made to files under the passed string ID since the first time it was downloaded (i.e. a change has been made to a GPML topology file on the Müller et al. 2019 plate model), then DataServer will now recognise this and update the cached file(s) accordingly.

All Notebooks 1-8 have been rerun to test this change, and figures for publication have been updated for review.

author: deploy-code-org
body:
# I18n Sync In & Up

This PR contains all changes to internationalization source strings made since the last sync (usually a week).

## To Review:

1. Look through the changes in each of the commits and verify that all changes are expected

   - We expect content changes to come in on a regular basis; individual strings will get updated, added, and deleted.

   - We _do not_ usually expect to see "comprehensive" changes - or changes that apply to large numbers of strings or whole categories of strings all at once - unless we have made specific code changes.

2. Notify the International Partners team about any changes that might appear to manifest as "lost translations"

   - For example: https://github.com/code-dot-org/code-dot-org/pull/31031/files#diff-aa1910a8cf8f9290ae3baf7e39dbae3eL397-R398

     This is a change that added new strings (with both new keys and new content) and simultaneously removed some very similar old ones; we can reasonably infer that the intent here was to swap the new strings out for the old ones. Unfortunately, because the swap also included a content change to the strings the crowdin duplication system won't automatically apply translations to the new strings and so they will need to be manually re-translated.

## To Deploy:

Once one or two people have reviewed and approved this change and the tests are passing, ship it!

It's not necessary to wait for everyone on the team to review.

author: johnwikman
body:
Previously, nested recursive lets would not get their entire body checked for free variables, which meant that the following function could not be properly lifted:
```
let foo = lam x. lam y. lam mylist.
  if eqi x 10 then
    ()
  else
    recursive let inner_foo = lam z.
      if eqi y z then
        inner_foo (addi z 1)
      else
        recursive let deep_foo = lam i.
          if eqi i z then
            ()
          else
            -- mylist is not mentioned in the parent reclet's body
            get mylist i;
            deep_foo (addi i 1)
        in
        deep_foo 0
    in
    inner_foo 10
in
foo 11 12 [1,2,3]
```

Added the example above as a test case. It failed prior to applying the fix in `findFreeVariablesInBody` (now passes as expected).

author: vinnl
body:
Rather than having a test depend on a value implicitly set in the
function, the test now explicitly passes the value it's matching on
into the mock creator. This can avoid the test accidentally passing
if the mocks are changed in the future. (For example, for this test
specifically, it's checking whether the string `some` is in a
mocked email's subdomain, but it would also succeed if that string

author: wufniks
body: With current implementation of `wasm-scheduler` you will get error like following when you use interval operator. As far as I understand, this is because 1. `interval` operator uses `scheduler_repeating` function of `LocalScheduler` trait. 2. Default implementation of `scheduler_repeating` uses `std::time::Instant::now()`. Once in the function body, another in the implementation of `async_std::stream::interval`. 3. We cannot use `std::time::Instant::now()` in the WASM(I am just assuming this following [this README](https://github.com/sebcrozet/instant#instant). Let me know if I am wrong) My suggestion here is that using `fluvio-wasm-timer` library. When we use this library in other platforms, it will re-export `std::time::Instant`. If we use it for WASM, it will provide us WASM-compatible implementations of `Interval`, `Instant` and extras. NOTE: You can get the code for the test [here](https://github.com/wufniks/wasm-rxrust) if you want.

In addition I have added a tracing span per call so it's possible to just trace specific method calls which could be quite useful I reckon.

For batches it's possible to just `log/trace` by the target `batch` because the span is called `batch` so not possible to trace the individual calls inside it.

author: infinite-persistence
body:
## Issue
Ticket: #108

## Interesting
Uploads Page uses `claim_list`
Channel Page uses `claim_search`

A second `claim_list` would instantly show updated results, but `claim_search` takes a long while to reflect the deletion.  If both are waiting for a transaction, why did `claim_list` work as expected?

## Change
This PR only handles the `claim_list` (Uploads Page).

## Aside
The `claim_search` version would be troublesome to handle. If a refresh would bring back the results (due to the `claim_search` slow update behavior), we would need to store the deleted claim persistently. Then ...
  - Store where? rehydrate?
  - When to clear?
  - How to make each `ClaimList` filter this out without polluting the code? etc.

...will be messy. Feels easier to "fix" at the `claim_search` to make it update faster like `claim_list`.

This PR adds the option to install Inertia React in Typescript. Adds ``react-ts`` option to ``breeze:install``. 

I've always wanted an easy way to quickly install Breeze with the Inertia React stack, but I prefer to write my code in Typescript. So, I put this together and decided to share as I'm sure I'm not the only one who prefer their code in Typescript. 

##### Example
```
$ php artisan breeze:install react-ts
```

The TSX components are copy and pasted from the regular JSX components, file extension changed to .tsx, and the appropriate types added.

The only two files changed, tested, and working are:
- src/Console/InstallCommand.php 
- src/Console/InstallsInertiaStacks.php


### src/Console/InstallCommand.php
Updates $signature to include react-ts example. 
```php
    protected $signature = 'breeze:install {stack=blade : The development stack that should be installed (blade,react,react-ts,vue,api)}
                            {--inertia : Indicate that the Vue Inertia stack should be installed (Deprecated)}
                            {--pest : Indicate that Pest should be installed}
```

```php
    public function handle()
    {
        if ($this->option('inertia') || $this->argument('stack') === 'vue') {
            return $this->installInertiaVueStack();
        } elseif ($this->argument('stack') === 'react') {
            return $this->installInertiaReactStack();

        } elseif ($this->argument('stack') === 'api') {
            return $this->installApiStack();
        } else {
            return $this->installBladeStack();
        }
    }
```

author: isobelhooper
body:
Currently, `expires_extra_ms` in arq/connections.py sets a default expiry of 1 day from when a job was expected to start to when it would expire if no expiry was set in `enqueue_job()`.

Our project found we needed that to be longer, so we made it configurable as part of both ArqRedis and Worker, as `.default_job_expiry`.

This PR also moves `expires_extra_ms` to arq/constants.py along with other shared constants.

----

`default_job_expiry` might not be the best name for this option, as it's one of a few different job expiry times, so I'm happy to rename the option as necessary.

Recent luarocks (3.8.0) autoreplaces `git://` with `git+https://`, but we have older luarocks version shipped with tarantool. See https://github.com/tarantool/tarantool/issues/6597 for details.

```
(Optional) Datadog cuts inactive connections after a period of inactivity. Some Rsyslog versions are not able to reconnect properly when necessary. To mitigate this issue, use time markers so the connection never stops. To achieve this, add the following 2 lines in your Rsyslog configuration:

$ModLoad immark
$MarkMessagePeriod 20
And don’t forget to restart:
```

It would be nice to have the same for journalpump

The language files now have an interface which makes it easier for developers to use the language files, and they have been sorted alphabetically by key.

Spanish and English translations are now in sync (all keys exist in both files) and the missing/incorrect keys have been also added to the relevant svelte components.

Following the example of https://github.com/sveltejs/realworld, they use the /lib folder simply as a separation between routes and hooks, but it doesn't only contain components; this commits introduces a lib/components folder where the .svelte components live (those that are not routes/pages).

Other changes include

* Add a prettier plugin to sort imports
* Create a i18n (internationalization) module which deals with language.
* Create a storage module and transform the helper methods into a class   which implements an IStorage interface
* Refactor the security module as to properly separate concerns (security module should not know about a Stellar KeyPair or the concept of a Stellar Private Key)
* Refactor the wallets, taking them out of the /ui folder and placing them in the wallets module, where they act as a Service
* Create a Stellar module which contains information about networks and passphrases imported from env vars rather than using the env vars directly
* Translate hide key/show key
* Add esnext as build target to enable top level await
* Create Bridge module which is responsible for managing messages between the parent window and simple signer. This is still not in an ideal state but it dictates a clear path moving forward.

author: florimondmanca
body:
Petite amélioration "expérience dev" du setup Ansible

## Motivation

Actuellement lorsqu'on déploie, la tâche de migrations est toujours marquée comme "changed" :

```console
TASK [web : Ensure migrations are up to date] ***************************************
changed: [localhost]
```

Et ce même si aucune migration n'a été lancée car elles seraient déjà à jour, avec ce genre d'output :

```console
$ make migrate
venv/bin/alembic upgrade head
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Context impl PostgresqlImpl.
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Will assume transactional DDL.
```

Ce qui ne contribue pas à un retour fidèle

## Description

Cette PR ajoute une option `changed_when` pour ne marquer la tâche comme "changed" que si une migration a effectivement été appliquée, avec ce genre d'output :

```console
$ make migrate
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Context impl PostgresqlImpl.
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Will assume transactional DDL.
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Running upgrade d694d065978d -> 67a6c2bf0696, add-dataset-contact-emails
```

Ça permet juste d'avoir un retour plus fidèle des changements appliqués lors du déploiement.

## Test

Testé sur la VM de test : 

- Lancer `venv/bin/alembic downgrade head-1` pour avoir une migration à appliquer
- Lancer le déploiement `make deploy env=test`
- La tâche migrate est `changed`
- Lancer le déploiement à nouveau
- La tâche migrate est `ok`

## Autres

N.B. : D'autres tâches sont toujours marquées comme changed, je les note pour référence. 1/ `Node dependencies` est toujours `changed` mais c'est une limite du module `ansible.community.npm`. 2/ `make build` est toujours `changed`, en théorie on devrait pouvoir se baser sur le commit hash.

author: psrok1
body:
Already existing implementation of blob reporting in MWDB uses different name of field that stores blob type:

https://github.com/CERT-Polska/mwdb-core/blob/0c2703da35436b7124ade36f75457dd17739e324/mwdb/core/karton.py#L82-L95
```python
def send_blob_to_karton(blob) -> str:
    producer = get_karton_producer()
    task = Task(
        headers={"type": "blob", "kind": blob.blob_type},
        payload={
            "content": blob.content,
            "dhash": blob.dhash,
            "attributes": blob.get_attributes(as_dict=True, check_permissions=False),
        },
    )
    producer.send_task(task)

    logger.info("Blob sent to Karton with %s", task.root_uid)
    return task.root_uid
```

As blob support is not yet included in stable release of karton-mwdb-reporter, we decided to make a change compatible with existing implementation in MWDB.

Adapt to the refactor of GetValues in oops https://github.com/JCSDA-internal/oops/pull/1680

<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title above. -->
(replaces closed #1739)

Various problems with single-response-requests existed as a result of their having a separate control
path from streaming requests.  Single-response-requests are really just special cases of streaming requests
that deliver __at most__ one `Next` message and need to behave as such.

<!--- This template is entirely optional and can be removed, but is here to help both you and us. -->
<!--- Anything on lines wrapped in comments like these will not show up in the final text. -->

single-response-request are now handled as *tasks* and can be overlapped with other requests
on the same connection, can be cancelled, and share the same unique requests ID namespace.

author: patricktasse
body:
Add a child container to TimeGraphLayer. Add children to the child
container instead of the layer container.

Destroy the layer and its children graphics objects in one call instead
of destroying each child component one-by-one.

When removing all children, destroy the child container in one
operation, destroying all children graphics objects.

The TimeGraphComponent.destroy() method is no longer called recursively
on the child components when destroying the layer or removing all
children. Components are not expected to have any local resources to
release at destruction, other than the graphics object.

Make TimeGraphComponent.destroy() also destroy all children graphics
objects of the component in one operation. Remove the now unnecessary
override of destroy() in TimeGraphArrowComponent.

In TimeGraphNavigatorHandle, add document listener in the mouse down
handler, and remove the document listener in the mouse up handler.

Fixes https://github.com/eclipse-cdt-cloud/timeline-chart/issues/187.

Signed-off-by: Patrick Tasse <patrick.tasse@gmail.com>

author: tlater
body:
###### Description of changes

Bump the driver version to the latest stable version to fix incompatibility with Linux 5.17.1.

I realize 22.05 is right around the corner, but I'd very much like to update my systems over the next 8 weeks, especially considering the recent zlib vulnerability.

Note that this steps through [510.47.03](https://www.nvidia.com/Download/driverResults.aspx/186156/en-us), which does raise the minimum kernel version (though we don't have kernels as old as 2.x anyway), and also removes some features (which had already been deprecated and unsupported). Subsequent releases, including [510.60.02](https://www.nvidia.com/Download/driverResults.aspx/187162/en-us) itself were bug-fix releases and should be updated to if we update at all.

I'm not sure if this counts as a breaking change as a result, however currently the driver is completely incompatible with `linuxPackages_latest`, so this may comply with the package update requirements anyway. If it's more appropriate to localize the update to 5.17.1 somehow, I'd be happy to do that instead, but I don't think the kernel packaging mechanisms currently support that?

###### Things done

I have also tested against both 5.17.1 and 5.10 (latest and default, respectively), including boot and running some games via proton, but this doesn't cover any of the more enterprise use cases a la cuda.

author: mdickinson
body:
There's a profiling script at the end of `scimath.interpolate.interpolate`, but running this script via `python -m scimath.interpolate.interpolate` produces the following slightly worrying warning about "unpredictable behaviour".

```python
(scimath) mdickinson@mirzakhani scimath % python -m scimath.interpolate.interpolate
/opt/local/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.8/lib/python3.8/runpy.py:127: RuntimeWarning: 'scimath.interpolate.interpolate' found in sys.modules after import of package 'scimath.interpolate', but prior to execution of 'scimath.interpolate.interpolate'; this may result in unpredictable behaviour
  warn(RuntimeWarning(msg))
```

After adding some `print` statements for debugging purposes, it's possible to verify that`python -m scimath.interpolate.interpolate` does indeed execute the code in `scimath/interpolate/interpolate.py` twice. (In this particular case that doesn't have any obviously bad side-effects, but the warning is still worrying, and it's easy to fix.)

~This PR moves the profiling script to its own module. To run the profiling script, run `python -m scimath.interpolate.profile`, which should now be warning-free.~

EDIT: Following discussion, this PR simply deletes the profiling code.

Review of threading safety (ONEMPERS-397) shows that there are multiple places where rdk plugins state can
be concurrently accessed by parallel threads, without any locking. This PR adds 'apiLock' mutex per plugin,
that assures synchronisation (and serialization) of API method calls & IARM event handlers, to avoid concurrency issues.
Updated plugins are:
LgiDisplaySettings/DisplaySettings
LgiHdmiCec
LgiHdcpProfile/HdcpProfile
XCast

By submitting a PR to this repository, you agree to the terms within the [Checkmarx Code of Conduct](https://github.com/checkmarx-ltd/open-source-template/blob/master/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md). Please see the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/checkmarx-ltd/open-source-template/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to create and submit a high-quality PR for this repo.

### Description

**Describe the problem**
Currently there is no way to filter only SCA vulnerabilities that breach Policy Violations

**Solution**
Add a filter-policy-violation config to the sca block that only validates vulnerabilities that breach Policy Violations:
````
sca:
  - filter-policy-violation: true
 ````
This will allow to create bug-tracking tickets only in cae SCA vulnerabilities breach policies.

If filter not configured then package policy violation, both true and false, will included in vulnerabilities.

author: lukaspaczos
body:
### Description
<!--
Include issue references (e.g., fixes [#issue](link))
Include necessary implementation details (e.g. I opted to use this algorithm because ... and test it in this way ...).
-->

Opening as a draft while I work on docs and tests (there are some debug logs that you can ignore as well). This branch also depends on eventual bump of Nav Native, currently based on a snapshot.

This PR introduces `AlternativeRouteMetadata` (and its children) that describe metadata of an alternative route, this includes the precise geometry indices of the fork with the primary, as well as summed duration and distance values.

These values allow us to precisely determine the point until which the alternative route should be vanished to avoid and overlap with the primary route which had a side effect of resurfacing when the vanishing route line feature was enabled.

_Before_:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16925074/161552866-6f1ba0ef-d0d8-4ad1-a925-52e4442f5e7e.mp4

_After_:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16925074/161552830-9ba6dda9-6abe-40c6-88db-3dd9f9149fe4.mp4

#### How

The alternative metadata is exposed via `MapboxNavigation#getAlternativeMetadataFor(NavigationRoute)` function. The idea is that each `NavigationRoute` reference returned by Nav SDK via `RouteObserver` (excluding the primary route) and `NavigationRouteAlternativesObserver` will have alternative metadata available via the getter function at the point in time when it's delivered to the developer - this is our guarantee.

In order to be able to obtain the alternative route metadata, we first need to round-trip it through the native navigator to establish the relationship and do the calculations. This pushes the timing of the observers (especially `RouteObserver`) significantly. Previously, the `RouteObserver` was called nearly immediately and only after that routes were set to the native navigator. Now, we're reversing the flow - we first set the routes to the native navigator, capture and cache metadata results, and only then call the `RouteObserver` to guarantee that the metadata will be accessible if available.

A side effect of this is that we need to wait for all the routes to be successfully set to the native navigator before delivering `RouteProgress`, not only the primary route. Since we don't want to deliver `RouteProgress` updates before `RoutesObserver` update was dispatched, we are adding a delay before the first `RouteProgress` update is actually delivered that is equal to the time needed to process alternative routes.

#### Next iterations
There are a couple of problems in the current proposal that I'd like to iterate on and follow up separately:
1. The fact that we need to wait for alternatives to be processed before dispatching `RouteProgress` also bears a risk of skipping some initial progress updates altogether (if they are returned while alternatives are being processed). My idea is to add a channel that will buffer updates received during the alternatives processing and deliver them sequentially after the routes are processed.
2. Since the `RoutesObserver` now wait for native navigator, we can actually refactor the codebase to only return back routes which were successfully processed by Nav Native, and remove the ones that failed.
3. As you can see in the videos, there's a problem with the route geometries briefly flashing, especially during the manual route switch. This problems seems to be reproducible on `main` as well, just much less pronounced since the route does not vanish in the first place.
4. The new `AlternativeRouteMetadata` goes out-of-date whenever `RoutesObserver` or `NavigationRouteAlternativesObserver` fires and is documented as such but I'm wondering whether we should bake in a `isValid` flag into the metadata instances to better surface this state. Additionally, this open up a question whether `NavigationRouteAlternativesObserver` should invalidate the metadata at all, it might just be need to invalidate metadata when `MapboxNavigation#setRoutes` is called and the primary route changes.

cc @SiarheiFedartsou @DenisPryt

### JIRA ### Referenced pull requests - https://github.com/kiegroup/optaplanner/pull/1919 - https://github.com/kiegroup/optaplanner-quickstarts/pull/318 ### Checklist - [ ] Documentation updated if applicable. - [ ] Upgrade recipe provided if applicable.
How to replicate CI configuration locally? Build Chain tool does "simple" maven build(s), the builds are just Maven commands, but because the repositories relates and depends on each other and any change in API or class method could affect several of those repositories there is a need to use [build-chain tool](https://github.com/kiegroup/github-action-build-chain) to handle cross repository builds and be sure that we always use latest version of the code for each repository. author: christophe-david
body:
Closes #404.

- Documentation has been updated.  Preview [here](https://fast-oad.readthedocs.io/en/mission-fixes/documentation/mission_module/index.html)
  - Description of mission definition and segments has been update
  - A section has been added about extensibility. Description of FlightPoint class has been moved in there.
- `FlightSegment._get_gamma_and_acceleration()` now take a FlightPoint as input, to allow the calculation to depend on more parameters than mass, drag and thrust
- a parameter with a variable as value can now be associated to a unit and a default value that will be used in the OpenMDAO input declaration (and be in generated input data file)
- a target parameter can be declared as relative to the start point of the segment by prefixing the parameter name with `delta_`
- when setting a parameter, a minus sign can be put before a variable name to get the opposite value (can be useful with relative values)
- a parameter can now be set at route or mission level
- dISA can now be set in mission definition file with `isa_offset`
- taxi-out and takeoff are now set in mission definition file:
  - mission starting point (altitude, speed, mass) can now be set using the "start" segment
  - the mass input of the mission can be set using the "mass input" segment. This segment can be anywhere in the mission, though it is expected that fuel consumption in previous segments is mass-independent.
- a mission phase can now contain other phases 
- if a segment parameter (dataclass field) is an array or a list, the associated variable in mission file will be declared with `shape_by_conn=True`

author: seokho-son
body:
This PR is to update localization.md to guide  to use both native and English names in `config.toml` to resolve #31657.

Some languages (Chinese, Korean and Japanese) are using both their own alphabets and Latin script in languageName (ex: `languageName = "한국어 Korean"`), but the others are using own native script only.

This inconsistency issue was discussed in Kube SIG Docs localization meeting Monday 2/7, 2022. And we decided a new recommended best practice using both native script and Latin (ex: "한국어 Korean") as it help folks who can't read native alphabets to know which language it is.

- I'd like to suggest a format for consistency: `"language name in native script (language name in Latin script)"` to `languageName`
  - languageName = "中文 (Chinese)"
  - languageName = "한국어 (Korean)"
  - languageName ="Français (French)"
  - languageName = "हिन्दी (Hindi)"
- Also, add description and example for `languageNameLatinScript`

author: lnihlen
body: I realized my logic behind when to save a named value back to the heap was flawed. Because of the dynamic nature of SuperCollider dispatch, in combination with lexical scoping, the compiler can't be sure when some external code may modify named values. I have refactored the name resolution code to load and store named values in memory on every reference. This change simplifies the code and prioritizes correctness over speed. Eliminating redundant reads and writes will have to wait for an optimization PR later.

### Context
Currently the only way to fetch a dataset is to provide a URL pointing to a JSON file, this change
aims to allow client-code to directly provide this object instead of making an extra round-trip to

### Results
Before:
```javascript
reader.setUrl('data/index.json', { loadData: true }).then(() => {
 // ---
});
```
After:
```javascript
import dataset from "data/index.json";

reader.parseObject(dataset, { loadData: false, baseUrl: "data" }).then(() => {
  // ---
});
```

body:
## Pull Request Overview

- Introduces new API to start identification on a single Annotation:  `/api/v1/annotations/identify/GUID` (optionally can pass ES query for _matching-set_ on POST body)
- Sets default algorithm in the event no `idConfigs` value is provided during Sighting submission, so pipeline will complete
- Bonus tweak of json output (related to ident algorithms) of `/api/v1/site-settings/detection`

---
**REST API Updates**

Initiate Identification on a single Annotation.  Can _optionally_ include an Elasticsearch query on the body of the POST.  If not query is provided, the _default_ matching-set query will be used.  (Returns `{ "job_count": N }` with number of ID jobs successfully started.)

```
POST   /api/v1/annotations/identify/GUID
{
    "bool": {
        "filter": [ ...... ],
    }
}
```

## Summary and Scope

Initial 1.0 docs and scripts for Add, Remove, Replace and Move NCN.

## Issues and Related PRs

* Resolves [CASMPET-5341]([CASMPET-5341](https://jira-pro.its.hpecorp.net:8443/browse/CASMPET-5341))
* Change will also be needed in `release/1.2` after further testing
* Future work required by NA
* Documentation changes required in NA
* Merge with/before/after NA

## Testing

### Tested on:

* early/initial testing on mug (1.2) w/ 11 workers, 3 masters and 5 storage nodes
* fanta (1.0.11) with 3 masters, 3 workers and 3 workers (cabled for 4 workers and 4 storage)
* Lumi add ncn-w004 to TDS

### Test description:

Tested add, remove and replace - focusing on testing:
* adjusting the network
* allocating IPs
* adding & removing SLS, BSS and HSM data
* removing the NCN role, wiping and powering down
* booting and configuring the NCN
* redeploying services (for add/remove storage case)

Firmware update was not tested given fanta is Intel based, but the link to the firmware procedure is included in the docs.
Add/Remove Switch config is documented but was not tested except when initially adding the worker and storage to fanta.

author: pariahbot
body:
Original PR: https://github.com/tgstation/tgstation/pull/65704
-----
## About The Pull Request

I'm adding a new Traitor Final objective where you basically get a DNA scanner, that can only scan animals, but can mutate you into a space dragon when you inject yourself with Space Carp DNA.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53777086/160239638-614eb9f8-6e36-4af8-963c-690871063dbd.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53777086/160239717-4e352a52-047d-4d05-96b4-02bfc67ee1c1.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53777086/160239720-1f6afe6d-32b9-4a11-8bdc-9cc5134881f2.png)

A lot of the code here was copy & pasted from Romerol objective, so it's pretty easy to understand I hope.

## Why It's Good For The Game

There's been negative opinions about both Romerol and Battlecruiser, one of these criticisms is that they are the only two there are. I'd like to add more so there's more variety to it.

I also like this as it adds a way for Space Dragons to be player-spawned, I've already shown my distaste for midround ghost antagonists, as I feel they reward people for doing nothing, with a murderbone antag. Not that this solves any of my problems, but I can rest somewhat happier knowing there's a way for non-ghosts to get an antag like Space dragon. (It's why I really loved Blob infection's addition)

## Changelog

:cl:
fix: DNA Vault's DNA scanners no longer accept Plasmamen, Skeleton, and Golems as DNA.
expansion: A new Traitor Final objective has been added: Harvest the DNA of a Space Carp, and use it to turn yourself into a Space Dragon!
/:cl:

# Issue

We cannot upgrade the `node-fetch` dependency to `node-fetch@3` because it requires ESM enabled. For this reason, we had to remove the dependency to use another one (building, testing and maintaining a http client was requiring too much work). I chose `axios`.

Pros: it is widely used and has only one dependency.
Cons: it is still in `0.x.y`.

# Solution and steps

- [x] Uninstall `node-fetch` and install `axios`

- [x] Add/update/check tests.
- [x] Update/check the cli generators.

author: talestationbot
body:
Original PR: https://github.com/tgstation/tgstation/pull/65704
-----
## About The Pull Request

I'm adding a new Traitor Final objective where you basically get a DNA scanner, that can only scan animals, but can mutate you into a space dragon when you inject yourself with Space Carp DNA.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53777086/160239638-614eb9f8-6e36-4af8-963c-690871063dbd.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53777086/160239717-4e352a52-047d-4d05-96b4-02bfc67ee1c1.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53777086/160239720-1f6afe6d-32b9-4a11-8bdc-9cc5134881f2.png)

A lot of the code here was copy & pasted from Romerol objective, so it's pretty easy to understand I hope.

## Why It's Good For The Game

There's been negative opinions about both Romerol and Battlecruiser, one of these criticisms is that they are the only two there are. I'd like to add more so there's more variety to it.

I also like this as it adds a way for Space Dragons to be player-spawned, I've already shown my distaste for midround ghost antagonists, as I feel they reward people for doing nothing, with a murderbone antag. Not that this solves any of my problems, but I can rest somewhat happier knowing there's a way for non-ghosts to get an antag like Space dragon. (It's why I really loved Blob infection's addition)

## Changelog

:cl:
fix: DNA Vault's DNA scanners no longer accept Plasmamen, Skeleton, and Golems as DNA.
expansion: A new Traitor Final objective has been added: Harvest the DNA of a Space Carp, and use it to turn yourself into a Space Dragon!
/:cl:

author: yuzefovich
body:
Backport 3/3 commits from #79250.

/cc @cockroachdb/release

---

**rowexec: report memory and disk usage of join reader for EXPLAIN ANALYZE**

Release note (sql change): Memory and disk usage are now reported for
the lookup joins in EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

**rowexec: add a hint for memory budget errors in the join reader**

This commit adds a hint if a memory limit error is returned to the
client suggesting to increase the workmem cluster setting or session
variable.

Release note: None

**rowexec: improve join reader memory budget usage in some cases**

This commit improves the behavior of join reader ordering strategy when
it encounters a memory error. That strategy has two large memory users:
the disk-backed row container for the looked up rows, and the
two-dimensional int array that stores a mapping from an input row to
positions of all looked up rows corresponding to the input row in the
row container. Previously, it was possible to run into a scenario when
the row container uses most of the memory budget (but doesn't spill to
disk because it doesn't go above the limit), and then we'd get a memory
error when accounting for the int array. This is case is now fixed by
asking the row container to spill to disk if it hasn't already.

It still is possible for the query to error out eventually when the int
array on its own exceeds the memory limit.

Release note (bug fix): Previously, CockroachDB could run into "memory
budget exceeded" errors when performing lookup joins. This is now fixed
in some cases.

Jira issue: CRDB-14736

Release justification: bug fix.

Jira issue: CRDB-14739

author: tgaddair
body:
One issue with using Pandas or Dask DataFrames as inputs is preprocessing caching. Prior to this PR, DataFrame inputs would always require redoing the preprocessing even if the input DF hasn't changed.

This PR does not transparently solve this issue, but instead introduces a new wrapper class called `CacheableDataframe` which can be used to provide the necessary caching metadata for the DF manually.

For example:

```
dataset = CacheableDataframe(df=df, name=name, checksum=checksum)
model.train(dataset)
```

The `name` is the key that will be used to identify the entry in the cache. The `checksum` is what will be compared to determine whether the dataset has changed since it was last cached.

One application of this would be to load a table in a database into a Dask DF and then give it a `name` equal to the table name and a `chcksum` equal to the last modification time of the table.

## Description

This PR mainly covers the issue https://github.com/qgis/QGIS/issues/46393. It resolves some performance issues, provides user feedback and introduces project states:

- Introduce a progress dialog for extent calculation
(signals are sent from QgsOgrProvider:: to QgsProject:: where a QProgressDialog is shown)
- Introduce the project states NO_PROJECT, OPENING_PROJECT, OPENED_PROJECT, WRITING_PROJECT, CLOSING_PROJECT

- Reduce unnecessary and time consuming feature counts in testing condition if the dataprovider's extent shall be calculated

The code has been built and manually tested without remaining errors.

Some commits have not been very descriptive. This PR description tries to make up for it.

author: stevieamb
body:
### 1. What changed?
-An additional query key was added to the graphql query, so that the page could have the images from the api populate the front home page. Additionally, an additional prop was added to the pet card component so that the url could pass down to the img element.

### 2. Why is this change necessary?
- This change was necessary so that we would, after the user posts the animal they want to re-home, the home page needs to be able to show the picture that has been refetched from the API. So this change makes sure we are able to fetch data from the api, so that when we need to refetch from a mutation, we know that it'll automatically update the page with a new pet being available for adoption.

### 3. What changed technically that may impact others?
- Well, we are querying the images from the back-end, so we are hitting the back-end server to get the images, which might impact the back-end devs.

### 4. How do we test it?
- You can test it by clicking the link for the website, and then seeing the different images of the pets on the home page.

<!--
    Tag your PR title with the components that it touches along with
    the type of change
    E.g. "fix(orc8r): Fix reindexer race condition" or "feat(agw) ..."
-->

## Summary

This PR modifies federated integ test fab file to run FEG inside the Magma VM

The reason for that change is that FEG uses host netowrk mode. That mode is not supported properly on MAC so we can't access to FEG services port (so we can send grpc messages from the host). To allow us to send messages and configure grpc services like mock hss, we need to move FEG execution to Vagrant vm, where docker host network mode is supported

Note this will only impact federated integ test.

on federated integ test

author: emmalrussell
body:
## Description

Intermittent test failures appeared to be caused by the ErrorReportController unit test `can serialize request body`, because it mocks the FuelManager client instance, and this mock is not cleared for subsequent tests (see ticket mrc-3111). 

To avoid this, I moved the serialization test from ErrorReportControllerTests to a new unit test class for the FuelFlowClient, since that is where the serialization actually happens. Essentially, we just want to test that the client serializes the ErrorReport object to the expected json. The remaining ErrorReportControllerTests already implicitly check that `notifyTeams` is invoked from the controller, in the set-up of testFlowClient: https://github.com/mrc-ide/hint/blob/master/src/app/src/test/kotlin/org/imperial/mrc/hint/unit/controllers/ErrorReportControllerTests.kt#L122 

The client's basic functionality is tested already in an integration test class, so this test is just checking the serialization part implemented within the `notifyTeams` method, not that the json is subsequently posted as expected. 

My first idea was to spy on the sut's `postJson` method and check that it called that method on itself with the expected json string. However, because the method is protected, spy will not work. So instead I created a subclass of the client class for testing purposes, which overrides the `postJson` method and captures the parameters which can then be verified. 

To enable this, I had to mark `postJson` in the client class as `open` - I think this is less of a code smell than opening it up from protected to public in order to test.

do this automatically for us.

Updating `TargetFrameworks` condition value for MAUI project templates to be consistent with values from the Application Page "Target Windows Framework" property.

author: stevenheidel
body:
### Summary

This PR proposes the creation of a new working group, the Examples working group.

The description is reproduced in a formatted version below:

### Examples

**Objectives**: Create example compiler passes using the Python AST to surface additional
improvements to the spec, and to enlarge the library of OpenQASM 3.0 examples.

**Description**:
Some of the most interesting and important discussions about the OpenQASM 3.0 spec have originated
from groups who are implementing compilers. For example, issue #307 on the physical mapping of 
dynamically dereferenced qubits was inspired by work on integrating OpenQASM with another
pulse-level programming framework.

This working group will implement example compiler passes using the Python AST with the aim of
identifying and clarifying more parts of the language. The code produced could potentially be used
for a production compiler, but the constraints of a production compiler (eg. performance) will not
be a concern for this group. The primary purpose of these passes will be as an educational
reference.

**Questions**:
  - What are the most valuable compiler passes to tackle? Potentially interesting:
    - Resolving timing
    - Converting 'new-style' gates from #323 to 'old-style' gates

**Completion of WG**:
This working group will have completed its efforts when it has implemented ~3-5 compiler passes,
a similar amount of examples, and created a clear path for future contributions to these libraries
of examples.

author: shanehuntley
body:
When specifying hex strings, we run across cases where we want to specify that a byte in not a specific value.

eg.

`
  $want = " {  81 FE ?? ?? ?? ?? 7F }
  $dont_want = " { 81 FE ?? ?? ?? 00 7F }
`

This pull request adds a not operator (~) on bytes so you could specify:

`
    $want_and_dont_want = " {  81 FE ?? ?? ?? ~00 7F }
`

This seems to be pretty straightforward and useful. At the moment only individual bytes can be negated, but it could be easily expanded to cover negated masked bytes such a `~7?`

More complex would be expressing as a general construct so you can have things like `~(00 | 01)` but I'm not sure how far we want to go in expanding hex strings to be a complete regex language in it's own right.

## Proposed changes

Users are now able to use environment variables in yaml benchmark configuration files. This should allow for further automation of tests.

- Environment variables are allowed only for fields where the value is a primitive type (number or string).
- Environment variables start with the `$` symbol. The rest of the value is considered the variable name.
- Mixed literals and environment variables are not supported as values. A value is only an environment variable or a literal.

During execution, Test Harness will replace environment variables encounter in the configuration file by the corresponding value in the current execution environment (or empty string if variable is not defined). Errors for invalid values will be reported as usual.

author: italypaleale
body:
Sorry is this is so last-minute.

While writing the docs for manually creating the stored procedures for Cosmos DB (see: https://github.com/dapr/docs/issues/2325 ), I realized that I was going to have to include source code (the JS of the stored procedures) inside the docs. That was not ideal.

A better solution would be to just tell users to `curl` the JS source code of the stored procedures from a tag in this repository. However, currently the source of the stored procedures was included in a variable in a Go file, so it was not possible to fetch that code only. Using Go embeds allows maintaining the stored procedures' source code in a separate file and have it embedded at build time.

TL;DR: After this PR is merged and we have the source code of the stored procedures in a tag, users will be able to just do something like `curl -LO "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dapr/components-contrib/v1.7.0/state/azure/cosmosdb/storedprocedures/__dapr_v2__.js"` to get the source code of the stored procedure. This would significantly improve the quality of life of users following our docs.
